title: Summon Brieflet: Inline incident summary + escalation affordance prototype
creator: Evan Cho
description: Goal: Design a compact, keyboard-accessible 'Summon Brieflet' UI component surfaced on the alert/incident timeline and alert cards. The brieflet provides a one-click actionable summary for the current incident state, an SLO delta snapshot, an estimated incremental cost impact (last 1h), and clear escalation affordances (call, message, escalate, create postmortem). Deliver a high-fidelity Figma prototype, annotated microcopy for each action, and a developer handoff spec that includes accessibility notes and API contract assumptions for dynamic content (SLO delta, cost delta, primary responder). Background: customers frequently search for a single-pane summary during incidents — compact, consistent, low-noise. This surfaced brieflet should reduce context switching, speed handoffs, and make the cost/SLO impact visible during triage and escalation decisions. Constraints: must render in small widths (280–420px), support streaming updates (SSE/WebSocket), and respect RBAC: users without escalation rights see disabled actions with tooltip explaining why. Must support existing Console color tokens and not duplicate the full incident timeline.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Brieflet visual style matches Console tokens and adapts to Compact/Expanded list views without layout breakage.
AC-2: Figma prototype includes states: idle, streaming update, action-success, action-error, and disabled (no permission).
AC-3: Microcopy explains SLO delta and cost estimate lines in plain language; product-approved copy present in artifact.
AC-4: Component accessible via keyboard and screen readers: focusable actions, aria-live region for streaming changes, and contrast >= 4.5:1.
AC-5: Developer handoff includes expected API payload sample strings and runtime update cadence guidance.
AC-6: Usability testing (5 participants) shows median time-to-decision reduced by at least 20% in prototype scenario vs baseline.
AC-7: QA checklist for RBAC, live updates, and cost calculation rounding included in ticket and signed off by Eng lead.
decisions: DEC-01: Prefer a stacked compact layout (title, SLO delta, cost delta, actions) rather than inline badges to reduce horizontal overflow.
DEC-02: Show a 1-hour cost delta with a tooltip linking to the full cost breakdown — product asked for conservative estimate only.
DEC-03: Escalation actions map to existing Console endpoints (POST /incidents/:id/escalate and /contacts/call) to avoid new backend work.
DEC-04: When user lacks escalation permission, show a muted CTA with 'Request Escalation' flow instead of full action menu.
open_questions: Q-1: Should cost delta be absolute (USD) or relative (%); Finance prefers USD while PM leans to % for cross-account comparability.
Q-2: What is acceptable staleness for SLO delta? (currently prototyped at 30s).
Q-3: Is there an existing telemetry event for brieflet impressions or do we need new events for rollout metrics?
Q-4: Should the brieflet auto-collapse after an inactivity timeout (user preference) or persist until dismissed?
